speaker_role: Yale undergraduate admissions office (official channel; speaker not named in transcript)
key_insights: Essays and short answers are a chance to tell the committee something not visible elsewhere in the application.
A common experience is fine as a topic; what matters is why it was meaningful to the writer.
Unresolved or conflicted experiences can be a good subject because they reveal how you think.
Officers say they do not grade essays or assign points; they use them to get a fuller sense of personality.
A trusted reader is fine, but heavy edits by others can strip authenticity and voice.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Yale admissions staff state that essays are not scored or point-graded.
notable_or_distinctive: The explicit statement that essays are not graded and that unsettled experiences are acceptable subjects; otherwise fairly generic.
reliability_notes: Very short official-channel video, old (8y), high-level advice with no specifics; transcript is clean.
